question: Does this mechanism make a SINGLE skill produce a better website, or does it only pay off when running a fleet of agents?

mechanisms.problemSolved: Generic, interchangeable UI shipping without anyone naming why it is generic or what would make it product-specific.
mechanisms.mechanism: Single-pass review procedure: write a one-paragraph product lens (user, job, first-read object), collect 3-5 comparable reference patterns, fill a Design Contract naming density/hierarchy/interaction-model/forbidden-defaults, then audit the implementation against it and return a hard PASS or HOLD verdict (never a soft list of nice-to-haves).
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Forces the model to state product-specific constraints and explicitly name forbidden generic defaults before judging the UI, converting vague taste critique into checkable claims tied to visible states.
requiredContext: screenshots or rendered output at target viewports
mechanisms.outputImpact: Directly counters the measured house-style convergence (showcase 0/8) by requiring a named, per-project set of forbidden defaults instead of a shared default aesthetic.
failureModes: Reviewer invents forbidden defaults not grounded in real evidence
Could become a rubber-stamp if run in the same context that wrote the code (see orch-04)
conflicts: orch-03 (ui-designer.md) demonstrates the noun-list failure mode this procedure explicitly avoids
mechanisms.testMethod: Run the gate on a generated page and confirm it produces a PASS/HOLD with named forbidden-default violations, not generic praise/criticism.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Add as an optional self-review pass in SiteSmith's audit stage: produce the one-paragraph product lens + forbidden-defaults list before generation, then re-check the rendered output against it as a PASS/HOLD gate alongside scripts/verify.mjs.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Design decisions justified by taste ('feels clean') rather than by how a real visitor with a specific intent would actually read the page.
mechanisms.mechanism: Build one persona profile (search query, psychology, attachment style, fears), then simulate a scroll-by-scroll first read producing two voices per fold: raw persona monologue plus a framework-grounded analyst note (LIFT / Cialdini / Fogg), ending in a scored verdict and prioritised, fold-specific recommendations.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Forces concrete, falsifiable claims per fold ('I still don't know who these people are') instead of adjective-only critique, and ties every recommendation to a specific fold and framework rather than a generic aesthetic judgment.
requiredContext: one persona profile (can be inferred from the brief)
mechanisms.outputImpact: Improves conversion-relevant judgment (first-read clarity, trust signal placement) independent of visual style — orthogonal to the house-style risk, additive to it.
failureModes: Qualitative simulation only — source file itself flags this is not statistical evidence
Low value if the persona is generic instead of specific to the brief
mechanisms.testMethod: Run against one real brief's landing page and check whether at least one finding maps to a fold + framework citation the team did not already know.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Offer as an optional post-build QA step for conversion-oriented briefs (landing pages, e-commerce, lead-gen) — not mandatory for every site type.

mechanisms.problemSolved: N/A — this is a negative example, not a mechanism to adopt.
mechanisms.mechanism: Long bullet lists of nouns ('Motion design: Animation principles, Timing functions, Duration standards...') with no concrete technique, threshold, or worked example, plus a mandatory first step of querying a 'context-manager' subagent.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: It doesn't — this is exactly the token-heavy, decision-in-a-list shape that the 55-line frontend-design skill beat 59-40. Cited as evidence, not adopted.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Negative if imitated: bloats token budget without giving the model any executable judgment.
failureModes: Hard dependency on a non-existent subagent for context gathering
conflicts: Directly contradicts the frontend-design vs SiteSmith measured result

mechanisms.problemSolved: A model reviewing its own freshly-written output in the same context misses most of its own mistakes.
mechanisms.mechanism: Verify in a separate context from the one that produced the work — even without any other agent or fleet, a second pass with no memory of writing the code catches errors a same-context self-review does not.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Cited from a controlled multi-agent study (DeepMind x MIT, 180 configs) but the specific claim about self-grading blindness is agent-count-independent: it is about context continuity, not fleet size.
mechanisms.outputImpact: Improves defect-catch rate in the audit stage without requiring any orchestration platform.
failureModes: Easy to accidentally carry over context (same conversation) and lose the benefit
Not a substitute for scripts/verify.mjs's objective checks (screenshots, axe, console errors)
conflicts: The diamond/fan-out framing this point is embedded in (orch-05) is out of scope
mechanisms.testMethod: Compare defect catch-rate of same-context self-review vs a fresh-context re-read on the same generated page.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Run the audit/finish-gate step (orch-01) as a fresh invocation with only the rendered output as input, not appended to the generation transcript.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Coordinating independent work across multiple agents (research, drafting, verification) in a fleet.
mechanisms.mechanism: Split independent work into parallel workers, verify in a separate context per worker, merge under one owner; the 'stop rule' says only split work whose pieces never read each other's results — sequential work loses when split.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Valid mechanism for genuine multi-agent fleets; irrelevant to a single skill invoked once per site build, and duplicates the project's own context-diamond skill.
mechanisms.outputImpact: None for a single-skill website builder.
failureModes: Orchestration overhead with no fleet to coordinate
conflicts: Already implemented by this project's context-diamond skill; nothing new to import even if in scope

mechanisms.problemSolved: Coordinating a PM -> Architect -> Dev/QA loop -> Integration pipeline across separately-spawned specialist agents.
mechanisms.mechanism: A dedicated orchestrator agent that spawns other agent files, tracks pipeline phase/state, enforces retry limits (max 3 attempts) and quality gates between phases via JSON handoffs.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Only pays off when multiple distinct agent processes actually need coordinating; a single skill run once per build has no phases to hand off between.
requiredContext: a fleet of spawnable specialist agents
mechanisms.outputImpact: None for a single-skill website builder.
failureModes: Pure overhead with nothing to orchestrate

mechanisms.problemSolved: Coordinated multi-agent swarms, persistent semantic memory, learned model routing, and plugin ecosystem for large multi-session engineering work.
mechanisms.mechanism: npm package 'claude-flow': hierarchical/mesh agent swarms with 60+ specialized agents, 314 MCP tools (memory, swarm init, agent spawn, hooks, task lifecycle), a 3-tier deterministic->Haiku->Sonnet/Opus router, 30+ plugins.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Genuinely built for large, multi-agent, multi-session engineering platforms. Its own SKILL.md explicitly disclaims one-shot/single-agent use: 'Do NOT suggest ruflo for one-shot edits, simple bug fixes, or tasks a single agent can complete in one turn.'
requiredContext: a project running many coordinated agents across sessions
mechanisms.outputImpact: None for SiteSmith as a single skill invoked once per site.
failureModes: Orchestration overhead the source itself warns against for this exact use case
conflicts: Self-disclaiming: SKILL.md:21 rules out the SiteSmith use case in the source's own words

mechanisms.problemSolved: Cross-session recall of what an agent previously did/decided, via HNSW-indexed semantic vector memory.
mechanisms.mechanism: mcp__claude-flow__memory_* tools store and semantically retrieve prior decisions/patterns across sessions.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Sounds attractive as 'don't repeat mistakes,' but for a design tool it means 'let past design choices leak into unrelated new briefs' -- the same mechanism class implicated in SiteSmith's own measured house-style convergence (three unrelated briefs, one look, showcase 0/8).
mechanisms.outputImpact: Negative: actively works against style diversity across unrelated site builds, which is the opposite of what SiteSmith needs after its own convergence failure.
failureModes: Cross-project memory becomes an implicit house-style engine
conflicts: Directly conflicts with the showcase 0/8 finding this rebuild is meant to fix
mechanisms.testMethod: N/A -- reasoned rejection, not empirically tested here.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Faithfully matching a specific existing product/brand's look when a brief explicitly asks to emulate it, without guessing at missing details.
mechanisms.mechanism: Fixed extraction checklist run before any implementation: visual theme/atmosphere, colour palette with named roles + hover/active states, typography rules, component stylings, layout/spacing rules, elevation/shadow system, responsive breakpoints. Treats a missing category as a question to ask, not an assumption to invent.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Grounds a 'match this brand' brief in a specific external reference rather than the model's internal default aesthetic -- the checklist shape (not the tool) is what's portable.
requiredContext: a specific reference site/brand the brief names
access to inspect it (screenshot or fetched styles)
mechanisms.outputImpact: Useful only for the subset of briefs that explicitly ask to emulate a named existing product; irrelevant otherwise.
failureModes: Source depends on an external repo (VoltAgent/awesome-design-md) SiteSmith does not have and should not assume exists
Multi-agent JSON handoff protocol around the checklist is not portable and must be dropped
mechanisms.testMethod: Give the brief a named reference site and confirm the extracted checklist has no invented/guessed values in categories not actually observed.
mechanisms.sitesmithForm: Optional pre-generation step, own wording only (checklist categories, not the source's text): when a brief names a specific site/brand to emulate, extract these categories from what's actually observable before writing code; ask rather than invent for anything not observed.

mechanisms.problemSolved: Giving a fleet of specialist agents distinct personas/specialties to route work to.
mechanisms.mechanism: ~200 agent persona files across 15 divisions, each following Identity/Mission/Rules/Workflow/Deliverables/Communication-Style template, installed individually into an agent runtime and addressed by name ('activate Frontend Developer mode').
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Valid for a multi-agent product (this is literally what the repo is for); has no role in a single skill that has no other agents to route to or personas to switch between.
requiredContext: a runtime that installs and addresses multiple named agents
failureModes: N/A -- out of scope by construction

mechanisms.problemSolved: Building knowledge graphs (ontology, entity/relation/event extraction, fusion, GraphRAG serving) as agent memory.
mechanisms.mechanism: 9-stage pipeline for turning text into a queryable knowledge graph.
mechanisms.whyItWorks: Not applicable -- a website-building skill has no entities/relations/events to extract, model, or fuse. No output impact of any kind on SiteSmith.
